description: The `--provider opencode` seam already dispatches OpenCode (`engine/agent.sh` `_run_provider`: `opencode run [--model MODEL]`). But pointing a run at LOCAL / self-hosted inference — to run high-volume agentic testing at zero API cost, deliberately accepting lower coding quality — currently means knowing the right OpenCode + model + endpoint config by hand. This tasklist makes that a first-class, preset-driven "cost-avoidance" mode: a documented, named configuration that routes agent turns through the existing OpenCode dispatch against a configurable local endpoint, so an embedding host (Cuneiform's Riju agents) opts into cheap local execution with one switch. No new provider — a preset over the existing seam. Scope: `engine/agent.sh` (+ config resolution in `bin/chief`), `docs/`, and `test/provider.sh`.

userStories.title: A first-class local-inference preset
userStories.description: Add a named preset that resolves to the opencode dispatch against a configurable local endpoint/model, with honest degradation when unconfigured.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented, named preset (e.g. `--preset local` / `CHIEF_PRESET=local`, or a documented `CHIEF_PROVIDER=opencode` + model + endpoint env combination) configures a run to use OpenCode against a LOCAL / self-hosted inference endpoint; the endpoint and model are configurable via env with NO hard-coded host

When the required local config is absent, the run fails with a clear error naming exactly what to set (the `GEONAMES_USERNAME`-style optional-config pattern) — it never silently falls back to a paid provider
The preset composes with the existing provider/model plumbing (it ultimately sets provider=opencode + the local model), so `chief ps`/`monitor` show the resolved provider·model as they already do

userStories.title: Document it as a supported mode with the honest tradeoff
userStories.description: Embedding hosts (Cuneiform, formant, …) reference this mode; document what it's for and its cost.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/` documents the cost-avoidance / local-inference mode: its purpose (high-volume agentic testing without API cost), how to configure OpenCode for a local endpoint, and the single switch to enable it
The tradeoff is stated plainly — lower coding quality in exchange for zero marginal cost — so it is chosen deliberately, not by accident
`chief models opencode` (the existing command) is documented as the way to see the local models available

userStories.title: Test the preset resolution offline
userStories.description: Extend the existing provider test to prove the preset reaches the opencode dispatch with the local config — no real inference.
acceptanceCriteria: `test/provider.sh` is extended to assert the preset resolves to the opencode command builder with the configured local model/endpoint, using the existing offline test-double pattern (no network, no real model), the way it already asserts `--provider`/`--model` propagation
A negative case asserts the unconfigured preset errors with the actionable message rather than dispatching a paid provider
